title: Unveiling the potential: A systematic review of ChatGPT in transforming mathematics teaching and learning
venue: EURASIA Journal of Mathematics, Science and Technology Education
extended_summary:
This paper asks how ChatGPT has been used in mathematics education and what effects it has on student learning, engagement, and broader educational experiences. The authors frame the work as a systematic review, noting that the rapid emergence of generative AI has created both enthusiasm and concern about its role in mathematics teaching and learning, especially for tasks that require conceptual understanding, problem solving, and reasoning.

The review searched Google Scholar and, using PRISMA procedures, identified 31 studies on ChatGPT in mathematics education. The included studies span multiple educational levels and contexts, with evidence drawn from exploratory studies, surveys, case studies, prompt analyses, comparative analyses, quasi-experimental work, and reflective papers. The populations represented include elementary, middle school, high school, undergraduate, and graduate-level mathematics contexts, with both students and educators as users.

Across the reviewed literature, the authors conclude that ChatGPT can support personalized learning, provide immediate feedback, assist with lesson planning and question answering, and increase student motivation and engagement. However, the review also finds persistent limitations: ChatGPT struggles with complex mathematics, spatial geometry, derivatives, and higher-level reasoning, and over-reliance on the tool may weaken skill development when not balanced with teacher guidance. The paper’s overall conclusion is that ChatGPT is promising as a supplementary tool in mathematics education, but it should be used cautiously and in combination with human instruction.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic review using PRISMA and thematic synthesis, but it does not present a meta-analysis or a unified quantitative estimate. The underlying evidence base is heterogeneous and includes many exploratory, descriptive, and qualitative studies, so causal credibility is limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports modest-to-strong positive signals for middle school math accuracy in at least one included study, including 90% overall accuracy on exam questions, but findings are inconsistent across difficulty levels and topics. Because the overall evidence is mixed yet includes some sizable positive results for the priority population, the impact is best rated green.

interventions.use_case: Systematic review of ChatGPT use in mathematics teaching and learning, including chatbot-based problem solving, question answering, personalized support, and lesson-assistance for students and teachers.

finding.finding_summary: Across the reviewed studies, ChatGPT showed both strengths and clear limitations in mathematics performance. For example, Li et al. (2023) reported 90% overall accuracy on middle school math exam questions, while Dao and Le (2023) found 83% accuracy on low-difficulty questions but only 10% on higher-difficulty items; other studies noted errors on derivatives, spatial geometry, and complex equations.
finding.measure: Math problem-solving accuracy; exam-question accuracy; performance on mathematics tasks across difficulty levels
finding.study_size: n=31 studies reviewed (with primary empirical studies varying by paper)

finding.finding_summary: The review reports improved student motivation, learning interest, and engagement when ChatGPT was used in mathematics learning. Zafrullah et al. (2023) reported a learning-interest score of 80.33%, and the authors synthesize multiple studies as showing increased motivation and a more dynamic learning experience.
finding.measure: Learning interest, motivation, engagement, student attitudes
finding.study_size: n=31 studies reviewed; specific included studies vary

finding.finding_summary: Several studies suggest ChatGPT can support problem-solving, mathematical thinking, and self-regulation, but others show weaker performance than teacher instruction or incorrect solutions on more complex tasks. For example, the review cites gains in problem-solving and critical thinking in some studies, but Dasari et al. (2024) found lower performance among students who depended on ChatGPT compared with teacher-guided instruction.
finding.measure: Problem-solving performance, critical thinking, self-regulation, mathematical thinking
finding.study_size: n=31 studies reviewed; specific included studies vary

finding.finding_summary: The review finds that ChatGPT can reduce teacher workload by supporting lesson planning, generating explanations, answering questions, drafting assessments, and offering quick feedback. These benefits are described consistently across the included literature, though they are not quantified with effect sizes.
finding.measure: Teacher task support, lesson planning, assessment generation, response generation speed
